## Historical audit — S0083, visible chunk 1 of 3

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/generic_same_structured_evidence/C1/test/commons_155212263/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to this file’s JSONL lines and events. Neither the reference nor rendered images are visible in the supplied observations.

| Evidence | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| Student request, line 1 | The goal was a separate-mesh reconstruction from one indoor photograph, matching viewpoint, framing, geometry and materials. The student’s “old metalworking shop” interpretation is an inference, not independently verified scene content. |
| Student response and execution, lines 3–5 | The first program specified multiple grouped objects: walls/windows, bench, lathe, two wheel machines, anvil, drawer and smaller inventory. It specified colored materials, procedural wear, camera and lights. Assemblies contain constituent parts, but grouping and coordinates do not establish physical connections, contact, pose or visual accuracy. Step 1 timed out after 600 seconds, with empty output streams and no image: a **technical interruption**, not a diagnosed geometric or algorithmic failure. |
| Runner feedback and student repair, lines 6, 8–10 | The student received the timeout and instruction to preserve composition. The replacement removed nails and procedural material graphs, reduced primitives and ring resolution, and requested Eevee. Step 2 executed successfully and saved a render and blend file (line 10, characters [0,106230)). The log’s 16-sample rendering output does not establish that the requested engine setting controlled the fixed runner. The exact cause of the first timeout remains unproven. |
| Selection and review, lines 11–15 | Step 2 was selected. The next student request included the reference and step-2 render and asked for comparison (line 12, characters [0,147939)). The student reported that the bench was too distant and shallow, foreground objects too small and uncropped, and surfaces/shadows too pale. These are student assessments, not independent visual verification. The student changed camera position and target while retaining lens, lowered lights, darkened materials, restored procedural wear and added details; step 3 was executed. Its result is outside the visible chunk. |

**Input and exploration.** No teacher message, teacher diagnosis or teacher-proposed update is visible in this chunk; therefore teacher receipt and adoption are not established. The timeout and comparison prompts are runner feedback, not evidence of a teacher. The student independently produced the repair and subsequent visual-review revision; the recorded CLI sessions report no tool calls (lines 2, 7 and 13).

**Outcome and uncertainty.** Step 2 is a formally successful execution, not proof of a correct reconstruction. Final outcome, step-3 render, and any later selection are unknown. Multiple objects and materials are evidenced by code and execution logs, but image-space visibility, actual part connection, object pose, camera match, lighting quality and render artifacts cannot be verified here. No conclusion about unseen chunks or images is warranted.

**Lessons.** Transferably, a failed render should be distinguished from visual evidence; a simpler replacement can restore execution, though the responsible change here is unresolved. Task-specific hypotheses are the student’s camera/framing and pale-light diagnoses; whether their changes improved the scene remains unverified.
